entities.summary: Ambrose of Milan, canonized as Saint Ambrose, was a theologian and statesman who served as Bishop of Milan from 374 to 397. He played a crucial role in the formation of Christian doctrine during the 4th-century Milanese Synod, where he articulated the Nicene Creed. This creed would go on to shape the theological foundation of the Western Christian Church for centuries to come. Ambrose's influence extended beyond the realm of theology, as he also played a key role in the development of the early Christian church's organizational structure and administrative practices. His legacy can be seen in the numerous churches, monasteries, and bishoprics he founded, which continue to bear his name to this day. Ambrose's letters, which number over 1,000, provide valuable insights into the life of a 4th-century bishop and offer a unique window into the spiritual and intellectual currents of the time. Through his writings and actions, Ambrose helped to establish the bishop of Milan as a central figure in the governance of the Western Christian Church, a position that would be reinforced by the rise of the papacy in the centuries that followed. Ambrose's life and teachings continue to inspire devotion and scholarship, making him one of the most important figures of the early Christian period.
